items.title: Henry Russ Interview, 1972-01-18
items.q: And, uh, I played with that band quite a while... that's Eddie Jackson... Eddie Jackson was the manager.

ctx.x: He lived in Baton Rouge, I think. I don't know. I haven't seen him. He's got a brother named Nelson? Is that the one?

No, no. No. I haven't seen that boy in years. He got out to Middick World for some reason. He got out to Middick World. And, uh, I played with that band quite a while. So, after I left that band, I go to the Supreme Band. And then, that's Eddie Jackson, Peter Lacasse, Phil, Colbeck, Nick Nairn. Uh, we weren't even in the piano that much. I think old man Humphrey, not William Humphrey, his daddy.

items.title: Henry Russ Interview, 1972-01-18
items.q: That was Chairman's brother. Oh, yeah. He started to play in trombone. But he didn't, he didn't, he didn't stay with us, you know.

ctx.x: We see, we got drums, and we got bass and trumpet, and you played trombone? A saxophone?
That was Chairman's brother. Oh, yeah. He started to play in trombone. But he didn't, he didn't, he didn't stay with us, you know.
